title: KP14 vyg25 with the priced state's mean reversion kappa_y 0.35 -> 0.15 (half-life 55 months), nothing else changed
question: Does the speed of the priced state move the fair gap in KP14 (finding 12's BGN ladder), or is the gap flat in speed as the reduced-form screen predicts?
notes:
vyg25k15. kappa_y 0.15.

K3 (docs/NEXTUP.md item 1): vyg25 with ONE parameter changed, kappa_y, the mean-reversion speed of the priced state y. sigma_y = sqrt(2 kappa_y) moves with it so the stationary sd stays 1. Types, shares, exposures, bv_comp and gamma_v 2.5 are vyg25's.

WHY NOW. Two predictions disagree about this knob. (i) BGN's finding 12 -- the fair gap monotone in switching speed, -0.0038 -> +0.0025 -> +0.0079 -- says the gap should RISE with kappa_y. (ii) The reduced-form screen (docs/REDUCED_FORM.md, 2026-10-07): across a 60-cell half-life x price x curvature cross and a 10-seed speed ladder, the fair gap is FLAT in the state's half-life from 6 to 120 months and scales with the price of the state's risk and with curvature of the value footprint; vyg30k70 (kappa 0.7 AND gamma 3.0) came back at +0.0159 against vyg25's +0.0148 with room up 24%, which is consistent with price and not speed. This pair isolates kappa_y at vyg25's price.

IS IT CLEAN? Checked from parameters_kp14.py at these parameters before any solve (2026-10-07). The instantaneous premium by type at y = 0, gamma_v sigma_y dlogV/dy, is 1.7 / 6.2 / 13.1 %/yr at kappa 0.15, 1.7 / 6.4 / 13.9 at 0.35 (vyg25) and 1.5 / 5.6 / 12.3 at 0.70: the top-to-bottom spread moves by -7% / 0 / -11%, so the premium ladder is held to within 11% by kappa_y alone. A0 at y = 0 by type (4.06, 4.19, 4.37) / (4.05, 4.20, 4.39) / (4.09, 4.21, 4.39) and type_theta (1, 1.22, 1.57) / (1, 1.23, 1.61) / (1, 1.20, 1.54): the level footprint of the type in value is unchanged to within 4%. rho_ty and const_ty positive for every type, A0 finite and positive. The saturating Girsanov shift gamma_v sigma_y / kappa_y is 9.13 b / 5.98 b / 4.23 b; the W-form solve grid spans the Q-stationary distribution (y_solve -17.2..11.6 at 0.15), so it is inside the solver's domain.

HALF-LIVES. kappa_y 0.15: 55 months, 6.5 half-lives per 360-month window. 0.35 (vyg25): 24 months, 15. 0.70: 12 months, 30. The screen's cross spanned 6 to 120 months.

MEASURED FOOTPRINT OF THE TYPE, vyg30k70's ten saved panels (2026-10-07, scratch): in units of the within-type cross-sectional sd of log size, the type ladder enters log size as +2.28 x standardised exposure plus +0.10 x its square, with no dependence on y (slope +0.001, corr 0.01); type ordering by size is monotone in 100% of months. So KP14's economy is a LEVEL-footprint economy, not the rotating one docs/RESULTS.md:422 describes ('at y = 0 value does not reveal the type monotonically' does not hold at bv_comp 1.2). Whatever produces its gap is not the state-dependent visibility of the type.

PREDICTION (2026-10-07, before any solve; the screen's).
(a) Both economies have a positive fair gap at t >= 2.
(b) The fair gap is FLAT in kappa_y: |gap(k70) - gap(k15)| < 0.010 on the paired per-seed difference (same seed = same aggregate path offset and same firm draws), and neither differs from vyg25's +0.0148 by more than 0.010.
(c) room within 25% of vyg25's +0.0820 in both; SR_max between 0.35 and 0.75; oracle mean expected excess return between 2.5% and 9% a year.
(d) winning DKKM penalty interior in at least 8 of 10 seeds, or a flat tail on materiality.
FALSIFIED (the screen's speed claim is wrong in KP14) if the paired difference gap(k70) - gap(k15) exceeds +0.010 at t >= 2 across seeds: that is finding 12's prediction and would mean speed converts room in a structural model as it does not in the toy. If (c) fails the economy is off-calibration and nothing else in it should be read.

SOLVE CORRECTNESS GATE, required before any seed: every G type under the 1e-6 relative-residual gate; the CIR integral stage raises on lost density mass and must not; A(y) matches the risk-neutral closed form of tests/test_risk_neutral_pricing.py below 1e-4 AT THESE PARAMETERS; validate_vy.py shows realised and expected returns agreeing by type within sampling error (variants/klc/verify_solves.py, with BOP_VERIFY_KP_SPEC naming this spec).

PLATFORM. Built as one chain (G then integ) on Quest with variants/klc/solve_kp_klc.sh, so the integ id is the one these G bytes produce here. The G id is printed before the solve; the integ id is filled in after the build.
